name: Regulatory response

subjectOf.text: Traditional forward looking corporate governance systems adopt backward looking perspectives only after stable and optimal rules have emerged as suboptimal and require replacement or amendment.
subjectOf.abstract: Traditional forward-looking corporate governance systems may take backward-looking perspectives if and when stable and optimal rules emerge as suboptimal, requiring replacement and/or amendment of existing regulatory solutions.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Dynamic Regulation via Governmental Contracts (2014)
scope_conditions: traditional stable and presumptively optimal rulemaking infrastructure

subjectOf.text: Among advisers who factor the regulatory regime into fund sizing, the direction of adjustment is split: 18.2 percent would lower assets under management to avoid the regulatory hassle, while 27.3 percent would still increase AUM and another 27.3 percent seek the right size to cover expenses.
subjectOf.abstract: While 18.2% would lower their AUM to avoid the regulatory hassle, 27.3% would actually still want to increase their AUM. Another 27.3% indicated a desire to attain the right size to cover expenses.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Private Fund Industry Five Years after the Dodd-Frank Act – A Survey Study (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2732915
scope_conditions: respondents who answered yes to survey question 7

description: 2 claims in the published works of Wulf A. Kaal carry the concept tag 'regulatory-response'. Derived node: a roster, not an adjudicated definition.
